interest: This file offers valuable historical insight into both private American commercial ambitions in the Pacific theater as World War II ended and the economic administration of occupied Japan during the early Cold War. Lieutenant Leary's inquiry illustrates how U.S. servicemen anticipated commercial opportunities and concessions in captured Japanese territories, while the State Department's reply underscores the diplomatic uncertainty regarding the disposition of former Japanese island mandates prior to the creation of the UN Trust Territory. Furthermore, the 1949 documents illuminate the economic intersection between the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) and broader U.S. foreign policy, specifically demonstrating how Japanese non-ferrous mineral production was surveyed to support the European Recovery Program (Marshall Plan), alongside domestic occupation issues such as mining subsidies, agricultural damage compensation, and labor rationalization.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.63, spanning July 1945 to April 1949) contains correspondence, an airgram, and a telegram concerning mining, mineral resources, and concessions relating to Japan and former Japanese-controlled Pacific territories during the final weeks of World War II and the Allied occupation. The early materials from July 1945 address an inquiry submitted by U.S. Navy Lieutenant Dennis M. Leary, Jr. via Senator Harley M. Kilgore regarding postwar mineral leasing and operational rights on former Japanese-held Pacific islands, which the State Department deferred pending final international territorial settlements. The later documents from April 1949 focus on industrial policies and resource monitoring under the Allied occupation, including a dispatch on the financial and agricultural impacts of mining damage compensations and planned workforce reductions in Japan's mining sector, as well as an Economic Cooperation Administration (ECA) request transmitted to SCAP for comprehensive 1948–1949 production and consumption data on aluminum, copper, lead, and zinc to support the European Recovery Program (ERP).

subfiles.about: Senator Kilgore forwards an inquiry from Lieutenant Dennis M. Leary, Jr. to Secretary of State Byrnes requesting information on acquiring mining rights on formerly Japanese-held Pacific islands.
subfiles.summary: Senator Harley M. Kilgore writes to Secretary of State James F. Byrnes transmitting a letter from Lieutenant Dennis M. Leary, Jr. Kilgore asks the State Department to draft an appropriate duplicate response that he can forward to his correspondent. He also requests the return of Leary's original letter once it has served its purpose.
subfiles.title: Letter from Senator Harley M. Kilgore to Secretary of State James F. Byrnes

subfiles.about: Lieutenant Leary inquires about procedures for obtaining mining rights or operating existing Japanese mines on former Japanese-held Pacific islands after the war.
subfiles.summary: Lieutenant Dennis M. Leary, Jr., USNR, writes to Senator Harley M. Kilgore regarding valuable mineral deposits on Pacific islands formerly occupied by Japan. Leary states that he and an associate wish to acquire mining leases or authority to take over and improve existing Japanese mines once hostilities end. He asks for guidance on the proper government officials and agencies to contact, and concludes by offering personal condolences on the death of Senator Kilgore's wife.
subfiles.title: Letter from Lieutenant Dennis M. Leary, Jr. to Senator Harley M. Kilgore

subfiles.about: The Acting Secretary of State informs Senator Kilgore that determining commercial mining rights on former Japanese-held Pacific islands is premature pending final territorial settlements.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of State replies to Senator Kilgore's July 16 letter concerning Lieutenant Dennis M. Leary, Jr.'s mining proposal. The Department advises that it is too early to settle matters regarding private commercial enterprises on former Japanese-mandated Pacific islands until their ultimate disposition has been established. Kilgore is advised to suggest that Lieutenant Leary submit an inquiry at a later date when jurisdictional authorities are determined.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State to Senator Harley M. Kilgore

subfiles.about: An airgram report from Tokyo discusses mining damage payments to Japanese farmers and plans for labor rationalization in the Japanese mining industry.
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-91 from the U.S. Political Adviser / Diplomatic Mission in Tokyo reports on the economic dynamics of Japan's mining sector. It notes that mine operators pay indemnities to farmers whose lands are damaged by mining, but these costs are passed on to consumers or subsidized by the government, creating potential distortions in agricultural land use. The document also touches upon impending plans to streamline and reduce the workforce employed in the Japanese mining industry.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-91 from Tokyo on Japanese Mining Operations and Land Damage

subfiles.about: The Department of State instructs SCAP to supply statistical data on Japanese production and consumption of aluminum, copper, lead, and zinc for use by the Economic Cooperation Administration under the European Recovery Program.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State transmits a restricted telegram to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers in Tokyo on behalf of the Economic Cooperation Administration (ECA). In connection with programming short-supply commodities under the European Recovery Program (ERP), the ECA requests actual 1948 and estimated 1949 data on mine production, smelter output, and domestic consumption in Japan for aluminum, copper, lead, and zinc. SCAP is asked to confirm if these non-ferrous metal statistics can be provided.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 148 from Department of State to SCAP Tokyo on Non-Ferrous Metals Data
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
